translations.text: Daniel ua Líathaite, abbot (airchinnech) of Lismore, said this when the woman was entreating him. He was her soul-friend. She, however, was trying to seduce him. It was then that he said:
O woman, a blessing on you — do not say it! Let us think of the meeting of the everlasting Judgement. Decay comes to every creature: I dread going into the cold earth.

You are thinking of folly without the strength of goodness: it is plain that it is not wisdom you are practising. What you say will be empty talk: our death will have drawn nearer before it could come about.
Let us keep in mind the end that lies before us (a short course): if we vex the King here, we shall be repentant in the land beyond.
I will not sell heaven for sin; it will be repaid to me if we do it. Do not give, for something sweet, what you will not find either here or hereafter, O woman.
Let it go from you (so that it may bear fruit for you [?]); do not sell your share in heaven; go to your home under God's protection; take a blessing from me, O woman.
I am as you, you are as me: I fear, you fear the good Lord; you pray, and I will pray to the holy Lord: O woman, say nothing more.

Do not be hunting after something that is not good, for the Prince will cast you into perdition; you fear, I fear sinless Christ, so that I may not risk a curse, O woman. 'That will be true,' she said. She submitted to his constant way of life for as long as he lived.
